correctness.rationale: For the side-one regular pentagon, all three original-vertex distance orbits are explicit. Dihedral averaging of an arbitrary linear extension reduces its row to signed coefficients (a,b,c) with 2a+2b+c=1. Applying three 1-Lipschitz distance functions and the exact identity 2H0+2H1+H2=2(phi+1) yields the global lower bound L >= 2(phi+1)/(1+2u+w). The displayed positive coefficients attain equality in all three vertex-point orbits. Explicit mass transfers control the two possible midpoint-pair orbits, with strictly positive algebraic margins certified by outward rational intervals; lambda>1 controls the unchanged vertex pairs. The packaged checker also exactly enumerates 70 source-potential vertices and performs 2450 pair tests. No infinite-family inference from finite tests.

value.rationale: A natural exact relative projection constant of a regular pentagon with all side midpoints. Unlike a single point or a square, the odd-fivefold symmetry yields three coefficient orbits and a nontrivial simultaneous compatibility question. The exact positive optimizer has a three-witness sharp dual certificate and two strict coupling inequalities, giving reusable structural data beyond a numerical LP evaluation.
